policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'his garments became white' shows no number for the verb: English 'became' serves both the singular ἐγένετο and the plural ἐγένοντο with the neuter plural subject. Nothing in the verse or its notes distinguishes them.
ASV 'there appeared unto them Moses and Elijah' is number-neutral in English; both the singular ὤφθη and the plural ὤφθησαν yield exactly this rendering with a compound subject. No note bears on it.

r00 and r01 differ only in spacing after μετ᾽, and r02 only in the order of participle and prepositional phrase. ASV 'talking with him' renders all three identically; Greek word order is not recoverable from the English.
ASV 'I will make here three tabernacles' is first person singular, rendering ποιήσω. The hortatory plural ποιήσωμεν would require 'let us make', which the ASV does not have.
The readings differ only in whether μίαν precedes or follows Ἠλίᾳ. ASV 'and one for Elijah' matches the fixed English pattern of the preceding clauses either way; word order is not distinguished.
Order-only variant. ASV 'hear ye him' renders ἀκούετε αὐτοῦ and αὐτοῦ ἀκούετε alike, since English requires verb before object here.

All three readings supply the same three actions — coming, touching, speaking. ASV 'And Jesus came and touched them and said' coordinates them with 'and', which is the ASV's ordinary treatment of a circumstantial participle as well as of a finite verb, so it does not show which member of the chain was participial.

ASV 'save Jesus only' has one word, 'only', standing against μόνον; whether the preceding word was the intensive αὐτόν or the article τόν leaves no separate trace, since 'Jesus only' is the natural rendering of both. No note bears on it.

ASV 'until the Son of man be risen from the dead' uses the archaic intransitive perfect 'be risen', which is not a passive and so does not force the passive ἐγερθῇ over the active ἀναστῇ. No note bears on it.
ASV reads 'And his disciples asked him': the possessive 'his' renders αὐτοῦ, which the base lemma lacks.
ASV 'And he answered and said' names no subject; the added Ἰησοῦς would appear as 'Jesus', as it does elsewhere in the chapter (vv. 7, 17, 25).
ASV 'and said, Elijah indeed cometh' has no indirect object; the added αὐτοῖς would appear as 'unto them', as at v. 20 'he saith unto them'.
ASV 'Elijah indeed cometh, and shall restore all things' lacks any word for πρῶτον; 'first' is rendered where present in this chapter (v. 10 'must first come', v. 27 'that first cometh up').
ASV 'And when they were come to the multitude' must supply an English subject pronoun for the genitive absolute whether or not αὐτῶν stands in the Greek, so 'they' does not witness to the added word.
ASV 'and suffereth grievously' renders κακῶς πάσχει with the verb of suffering; κακῶς ἔχει is idiomatic for being ill and would give 'is grievously ill' rather than 'suffereth'.
Order-only variant. ASV 'how long shall I be with you?' fixes the English order independently of whether μεθ᾽ ὑμῶν precedes or follows ἔσομαι.
ASV 'And he saith unto them' has the pronoun subject and the present tense of λέγει; RP's Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν would give the named subject and past tense, 'And Jesus said unto them'.
ASV 'Because of your little faith' renders ὀλιγοπιστίαν; ἀπιστίαν is unbelief and would give 'because of your unbelief'.
The readings are equivalent forms of the same command and adverb. ASV 'Remove hence to yonder place' renders Μετάβα ἔνθεν and Μετάβηθι ἔντεῦθεν identically.

The ASV text of the chapter runs from v. 20 to v. 22 with no verse 21, and the mapped textual_variant note here credits the sentence to others — 'Many authorities, some ancient, insert verse 21' — so the ASV's own text is the shorter reading.

ASV 'while they abode in Galilee' renders ἀναστρεφομένων, and the mapped textual_variant note places the base reading in the margin: 'Some ancient authorities read were gathering themselves together' is συστρεφομένων.

ASV 'And when he came into the house' renders the aorist participle ἐλθόντα and the ὅτε clause with the finite εἰσῆλθεν alike; the temporal English clause is the ASV's normal treatment of both constructions.

ASV 'And when he said, From strangers, Jesus said unto him' has an unnamed subject in a subordinate clause, matching the genitive absolute εἰπόντος δέ; RP's Λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Πέτρος would give an independent clause naming Peter.
ASV 'go thou to the sea' requires the English definite article whether or not τὴν stands in the Greek, so the presence of the article is not distinguished.
ASV 'the fish that first cometh up' does not mark aspect: 'cometh up' serves the aorist ἀναβάντα and the present ἀναβαίνοντα alike in this relative clause.
